theses.thesis: NVIDIA will increasingly defend its AI infrastructure position by making NVLink/rack architecture a platform for third-party custom accelerators, not only by selling NVIDIA-designed GPUs.
theses.rationale: NVLink Fusion and the MediaTek partnership point toward monetizing interconnect and system architecture even when customers use custom compute dies. The September 9 Qualcomm-Amazon custom-silicon and optical-connectivity collaboration is useful counter-pressure: hyperscalers are simultaneously building alternative vertically integrated paths, so NVIDIA must win third-party XPU adoption rather than assume it. September 10 adds mixed but compatible evidence: NVIDIA is extending workload-specific serving architecture through Dynamo/EPD while China's accelerator ecosystem shows that memory supply and software portability can constrain platform control independently of compute silicon.
falsifiers: Major custom-XPU builders broadly reject NVLink Fusion in favor of open/alternative fabrics
NVLink Fusion sees little production adoption outside NVIDIA-centric systems
NVIDIA retreats from third-party XPU integration

evidence_updates.summary: Qualcomm and Amazon announced multi-generation custom AI silicon plus optical interconnect work for AWS. This does not falsify the thesis, but strengthens the competing-platform path NVIDIA must overcome.

NVIDIA Dynamo EPD extends NVIDIA's stack upward into multimodal serving architecture, while reported Chinese HBM pressure and multi-hardware software ecosystems reinforce that memory and portability remain alternative control points. Thesis remains active; confidence unchanged.

theses.thesis: By March 2027, at least two major frontier or enterprise AI platforms will expose customer-configurable runtime policies plus customer-controlled agent telemetry as first-class product primitives rather than keeping these controls only as vendor-internal safety systems.
theses.rationale: OpenAI is pairing Astra-class capability with gated access and runtime action monitoring; Anthropic is moving monitoring data into customer-controlled clouds with EFS; Microsoft is productizing agent identity, tool-policy and runtime controls; security vendors are integrating agent runtime protection into enterprise platforms. Meta's Muse provides a concrete externalized-authority pattern—isolated runtime, Sentinel egress policy, scoped approvals and credentials outside the agent—and AWS is making agent trace evaluation a CI quality gate through AgentCore. On September 10, Red Hat AI 3.5 adds platform-level guardrails/observability and the Visa/Mastercard/Ant Know-Your-Agent initiative strengthens the broader pattern of external identity, delegation and authorization layers.
falsifiers: Runtime policy and action monitoring remain mostly vendor-internal across major AI platforms through March 2027
Customer-controlled agent telemetry remains a niche or pilot-only feature without meaningful enterprise production adoption
Major providers retreat toward model-only refusals without exposing operational policy controls

evidence_updates.summary: Meta published Muse's Sentinel/secure-runtime architecture with user-scoped action approvals and egress enforcement. AWS separately published an AgentCore/GitHub Actions pattern for trace-based regression gates. These are supporting signals, although Muse is consumer-facing and the thesis remains unresolved.

Red Hat AI 3.5 explicitly positions guardrails, observability and controlled AI operations as platform primitives; payment networks are separately converging on agent identity and delegated intent. This strengthens the external-control-plane thesis without yet satisfying its March 2027 adoption criterion.
